metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL PostgreSQL OTel] Connection utilization high
metadata.description: Alerts when the average number of PostgreSQL backends on an instance is at or above 85% of max_connections over 15 minutes, for 2 consecutive checks. max_connections is not reported as a metric, so the query derives Cloud SQL's default from the instance memory tier; replace it with your value if you override the max_connections flag. Connection exhaustion makes new connections fail. Grouped by database_id.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_postgresql.otel-*
| WHERE gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// num_backends is a per-database gauge split by attributes.database AND by series
// fragmentation: sum it per minute first to get the instance total.
| STATS backends = SUM(MAX_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/postgresql/num_backends`)),
        mem_quota = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/memory/quota`))
    BY `@timestamp` = TBUCKET(1 minute), database_id
// Fill memory quota onto every minute of the instance (it is reported in the same minutes)
| INLINE STATS quota_bytes = MAX(mem_quota) BY database_id
// Only minutes with num_backends: this is also the PostgreSQL engine marker
| WHERE backends IS NOT NULL AND quota_bytes IS NOT NULL
| STATS avg_backends = AVG(backends),
        max_backends = MAX(backends),
        quota_bytes = MAX(quota_bytes),
        minutes = COUNT(*)
    BY database_id
// Default max_connections that Cloud SQL derives from instance memory (GB).
// Memory quota is slightly below the tier size, so boundaries are rounded down.
// If you override the max_connections database flag, replace this CASE with
// your configured value (e.g. EVAL max_conn = 500), or a per-instance CASE on database_id.
| EVAL mem_gb = quota_bytes / 1000000000.0
| EVAL max_conn = CASE(
    mem_gb < 1.0, 25,
    mem_gb < 3.5, 50,
    mem_gb < 5.8, 100,
    mem_gb < 7.3, 200,
    mem_gb < 14.5, 400,
    mem_gb < 29.0, 500,
    mem_gb < 58.0, 600,
    mem_gb < 116.0, 800,
    1000)
| EVAL conn_avg_pct = ROUND(avg_backends * 100.0 / max_conn, 1),
       conn_peak_pct = ROUND(max_backends * 100.0 / max_conn, 1)

data.content:
## Cloud SQL PostgreSQL connection utilization high

The instance is close to `max_connections`. When it is reached, new client connections are refused.

### Triage
1. Confirm the real limit: `SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_connections';`. The rule assumes the Cloud SQL default for the instance memory tier.
2. On the Instance Detail dashboard, check `num_backends_by_state`: many `idle` connections point to oversized client pools, many `idle in transaction` point to an application leak.
3. Check new connection rate for a connection storm (for example after a deploy or failover).
4. Mitigate with a connection pooler (PgBouncer, Cloud SQL Managed Connection Pooling), smaller client pools, or a larger tier.

### Tuning
- If you set the `max_connections` flag, replace the `max_conn` CASE with your configured value.
